database.sentence.pending: Being created. The node picks the change up on its next reconcile, and the connection details appear as soon as it confirms.
database.sentence.deleting: Being dropped. The node removes what is not in its spec, so this finishes even if it is offline right now.
database.sentence.failedDefault: The node could not create this database and did not say why.
database.sentence.suspended: Suspended. It still exists and still holds its data; nothing can connect to it until it is resumed.
database.sentence.overQuota: Over its size limit. Writes may start failing - raise the limit or free space in it.
database.sentence.nodeUnreachable: Serving normally. The panel has no control stream to its node at the moment, so rotating the password and dropping it are unavailable until that comes back.
database.sentence.unmeasured: Ready. The node has not measured its size yet, which it does on its own schedule.
database.engineSentence.unreported: The node has not reported on this container yet. That is a new engine, not a stopped one.
database.engineSentence.notConverged: Asked to be {desired}, and the node reports {reported}. It reconciles every fifteen seconds.
database.engineSentence.nodeUnreachable: Running. The panel has no control stream to its node, so nothing can be published to it right now.
database.engineSentence.stopped: Stopped, with its data directory left where it is.
database.list.title: Databases
database.list.description: PostgreSQL and MySQL, managed for you. Each one gets its own login, its own size limit and a connection string you can copy - and none of them is reachable from anywhere but your own services.
database.list.label: databases
database.list.emptyNoProjects.title: No databases yet
database.list.emptyNoProjects.descriptio: A database belongs to a project, so start from the project that needs it - open it, and create the database from there. Once you have one, this page lists every database you can reach.
database.list.empty.title: No databases yet
database.list.empty.description: Create one and the platform provisions it on the node your services already run on, with a login that can reach nothing else.
database.detail.where.title: Where it lives
database.detail.plan.title: Your plan
database.detail.plan.description: How many databases this organization may have, across every project.
database.form.create.title: New database
database.form.create.description: It is created on the engine already running on the node your project's services are placed on, with a login of its own that can reach nothing else.
database.form.create.projectHint: The database belongs to a project, which is what decides who can reach it.
database.form.create.name: Name
database.form.create.nameHint: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. This is the name you type back to drop it.
database.form.create.sizeLimitHint: Measured by the node on its own schedule. You can change it later without touching the data.
database.form.create.dedicated: Give this organization its own engine container
database.form.create.dedicatedHint: Shared is the default and it is the right answer for almost everything: a PostgreSQL container costs 30-50MB sitting idle, and one per customer does not scale. A dedicated instance isolates noisy neighbours at that cost.
database.conn.title: Connection details
database.conn.description: Shown on this screen only. Reloading the page loses them, and the panel keeps the password encrypted - ask again and it is a fresh audit entry, not a fresh password.
database.conn.copyUriAria: Copy the full connection URI including the password
database.conn.secretNotice: Put it in your service's secrets, not in a repository. A secret set on a service is not shown again either.
database.actions.title: Connecting to it
database.actions.readOnlyNotice: Your role in {org} is read-only, so the connection details and the password are not yours to reveal. Ask an owner or an administrator of the organization.
database.actions.description: Credentials are shown once and the panel records who asked.
database.actions.blockedStream: The panel has no control stream to {node} right now. The database keeps serving; these three need the node to answer.
database.actions.blockedInFlight: The platform is still working on this database. These become available when it settles.
database.actions.blockedState: This database is not in a state these can act on.
database.actions.rotateConfirm.title: Change the password for {name}?
database.actions.rotateConfirm.body: A new password is set immediately and the old one stops working. Anything connected with it - a running service, a cron job, your laptop - fails until it is updated. The new password is shown once, on the page you come back to.
database.actions.dropConfirm.title: Drop {name}?
database.actions.dropConfirm.body: This deletes the database, its login and everything in it. The panel cannot get it back; a backup can, if you have one.
database.quota.title: Size
database.quota.description: Measured on the node. Raising the limit takes effect on the node's next reconcile; nothing is moved or rewritten.
database.quota.ariaUsed: {percent} per cent of the limit used
database.quota.pastLimit: This database is past its limit. Writes to it can start failing - raise the limit here, or delete data inside it.
database.quota.limitHint: Your organization's plan caps the total across every database it owns.
database.quota.readOnly: The limit is {limit}. Changing it needs a role that can write.
database.admin.title: Database engines
database.admin.description: One shared PostgreSQL and one shared MySQL per node, with a database and a login inside them per customer. Hundreds of separate containers would cost 30-50MB each sitting idle; a tenant who needs the isolation gets a dedicated instance.
database.admin.overQuotaDesc: These are what fills a node's disk. On a node without XFS project quota nothing stops them, so this list is the only warning there is.
database.admin.empty.title: No engine containers yet
database.admin.empty.description: None have been created, and that is normal on a new platform: the first customer who asks for a database gets one made for them on the node their services run on. Add one here if you would rather it were already running.
database.adminDetail.title: {engine} on {node}
database.adminDetail.desiredState.title: Desired state
database.adminDetail.desiredState.descri: The panel publishes what it wants; the node converges on it every fifteen seconds. Nothing here reaches into the machine.
database.adminDetail.askStop: Ask the node to stop it
database.adminDetail.askRun: Ask the node to run it

database.adminDetail.cannotRemove.one: It still holds 1 customer database, so it cannot be removed. Drop or move those first.
database.adminDetail.cannotRemove.other: It still holds {count} customer databases, so it cannot be removed. Drop or move those first.

database.adminDetail.stopConfirm.title: Stop {engine} on {node}?
database.adminDetail.stopConfirm.body: Every one of the {count} databases in this container stops accepting connections, and every application using them starts failing. The data is untouched and starting it again brings them back.
database.adminDetail.removeConfirm.title: Remove this engine from the node’s spec?
database.adminDetail.removeConfirm.body: The container goes away on the next reconcile. Its data directory on the node is left exactly where it is, so nothing is lost - but nothing will be serving it either.
database.adminDetail.facts.title: Facts
database.adminForm.title: Add an engine container
database.adminForm.description: It goes into the node's spec and starts on its next reconcile. One shared instance per engine per node is the design; customers get a database and a login inside it, not a container each.
database.adminForm.nodeIdHint: Open Nodes, pick the machine, and copy the node id from its facts.
database.adminForm.invalidNodeId: That is not a node id. Copy it from the node’s page under Nodes.
